claim_being_audited: That certifying the model for launch is compliant and evidentially supported despite the enterprise refund workflow gap.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the policy threshold is satisfied for certification.
A named launch use case or customer-commitment segment makes the weakness material under the provided policy text.
If the limitation is material, certification requires evidence of resolution, disclosure, or approved risk acceptance before launch.
Aggregate pass metrics and post-launch monitoring are secondary considerations and do not cure a missing policy-required approval or disclosure.
evidence_requests: Produce the launch disclosure that addresses the enterprise refund workflow limitation.
Produce the approved risk-acceptance record covering this named launch use case before launch.
Produce the final legal determination on whether disclosure is required.
Produce admissible evidence showing the affected segment is not a named launch use case or not tied to customer commitments, if that is the basis for certification.
Produce the governing release-policy excerpt and any exception approval relied on for this certification.
specific_concerns: The available policy text states a weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case.
The packet itself says the affected enterprise refund workflow segment is named in a renewal success plan, which points toward materiality rather than away from it.
The packet says legal review on disclosure is still pending, and the policy text says pending legal review does not resolve materiality.
No admissible evidence is provided showing the required disclosure was made before launch.
No admissible evidence is provided showing approved risk acceptance before launch.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not answer the policy predicate for a material named use-case limitation.
unsupported_claims: The claim that certification can be defended on the current admissible record.
Any implication that the 4% projected first-month traffic share makes the weakness immaterial under the stated policy.
Any implication that public model-card or NIST-style monitoring guidance is sufficient to override the release-policy requirement for disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
